issues.legal_issue: Pending consumer complaints filed under a repealed consumer-protection regime remain before the corresponding existing forum when the replacement regime changes pecuniary jurisdiction but does not indicate an intention to transfer pending cases.
material_facts: The complainants filed their consumer complaint under the earlier consumer-protection legislation before the replacement legislation came into force.
The claim fell below the higher pecuniary threshold for the national forum under the replacement legislation.
After the replacement legislation came into force, the national forum dismissed the complaint for want of pecuniary jurisdiction and later dismissed a review petition.
The replacement legislation changed the pecuniary limits of the consumer fora but did not expressly provide for transferring pending complaints under the new limits.
The legislation’s consumer-protection purpose and the hardship and disruption that transferring pending cases would cause weighed against inferring an intention to transfer them.
issues.conclusion: The complaint must continue before the national forum corresponding to the forum in which it was instituted under the earlier legislation; it is not to be transferred under the replacement legislation’s pecuniary limits. The appeals were allowed and the orders dismissing the complaint were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A change of forum is ordinarily procedural and applies to pending proceedings unless a contrary legislative intention appears. Sections 107(1)–(3) of the Consumer Protection Act 2019 repeal the earlier Act, preserve prior actions insofar as they are consistent with the new Act, and preserve the application of Section 6 of the General Clauses Act 1897. Section 6(c) preserves rights accrued under the repealed enactment, and Section 6(e) preserves proceedings to enforce such rights; those provisions do not, by themselves, preserve a right to a particular forum. The Court applied New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Smt Shanti Mishra, Maria Cristina De Souza v. Amria Zurana Pereira Pinto, Hitendra Vishnu Thakur v. State of Maharashtra, Sudhir G Angur v. M Sanjeev, and Ramesh Kumar Soni v. State of Maharashtra on the procedural character of changes in forum. It distinguished the substantive-right and accrued-right cases, including Garikapati Veeraya v. N Subbiah Choudhry and Ambalal Sarabhai Enterprises Ltd. v. Amrit Lal & Co., and declined to follow the contrary forum-as-vested-right approach in Commissioner of Income Tax, Orissa v. Dhadi Sahu, which had not considered the relevant larger-bench authority. The absence of a transfer direction, read with the statutory scheme and consumer-protection purpose, showed no contrary intention to transfer pending complaints.

rule.if: pending_consumer_complaint and filed_under_prior_regime and forum_pecuniary_limits_changed and not clear_transfer_intent

predicates.pending_consumer_complaint: A consumer complaint was pending before a consumer adjudicatory forum when the replacement regime came into force.
predicates.filed_under_prior_regime: The complainant instituted the complaint under the consumer-protection regime that preceded the replacement regime.
predicates.forum_pecuniary_limits_changed: The replacement regime changed the monetary thresholds determining which consumer forum could hear original complaints.
predicates.clear_transfer_intent: The legislature clearly directed, expressly or by necessary implication, that pending complaints be transferred to forums under the replacement regime.

issues.definition: When a consumer complaint was pending under the prior regime, the replacement regime changed forum thresholds, and no clear intention to transfer appears, the corresponding prior forum retains the case.
